diagnosis: Cellulitis of the left lower leg.
hospital_course: You came in with a red, warm, painful left lower leg and fever. Blood tests and an ultrasound showed an infection of the skin without a blood clot. You received IV antibiotics, the redness has started to shrink, and your fever is gone.

medications.name: Cephalexin
medications.note: Take it even if the leg looks better.

diet: Eat a normal, balanced diet with enough protein to help your skin heal.
activity: Keep your left leg raised on pillows above heart level when you sit or lie down.
Walk short distances every few hours. Avoid standing for long periods.
care: Wash the area gently with soap and water once a day and pat it dry.
Moisturize the dry skin around the area, but not on any open sore.
Wear clean, loose socks and shoes that do not rub.
monitoring: Use a pen to mark the edge of the redness today. Check the mark every morning and evening for 7 days to see if the redness spreads.
Check your temperature every evening for 7 days.

follow_up.purpose: a skin check and to review the redness

warning_signs: a fast heartbeat with shaking chills
skin turning purple or black, or blisters filling with dark fluid
severe pain far worse than the way the leg looks
call_clinic: redness spreading past the line you drew
a fever of 101 F (38.3 C) or higher
pus or drainage from the area
